question: Will N’Kiyla “Jasmine” Thomas be the Democratic nominee for Senate in Oklahoma?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Democratic Primary for United States Senator from Oklahoma.

If no 2026 Oklahoma Democratic Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Oklahoma Democratic Party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

evidence.excerpt: In the June primary, N’Kiyla Jasmine Thomas led the five-way Democratic primary with 45% of the vote, and Jim Priest followed with nearly 24%. State law requires a runoff when no candidate in a primary earns more than half the vote. Neither Thomas nor Priest has held elected office before. Priest, a lawyer and nonprofit executive, ran in 2010 to serve as state Attorney General and lost to Republican Scott Pruitt.

In an Aug. 25 runoff election, Oklahoma voters will choose the Democratic nominee to replace Markwayne Mullin in the U.S. Senate after his March appointment to lead the Department of Homeland Security. The winner of the runoff will face Republican Kevin Hern in the general election in November. Hern has served as the Congressman for Oklahoma’s first district since 2018 and swept the Republican primary in June.

Democrat: The race remains undecided, as N’Kiyla Jasmine Thomas (who received 45.2% of the vote) and Jim Priest (23.9%) head to a runoff. Thomas’ platform supports K-12 funding, universal healthcare and government transparency. Priest is an ordained minister and employment-law attorney in favor of keeping rural hospitals open and lowering the cost of living.

State Election Board Secretary Paul Ziriax announced today that no political party filed a notice to allow Independents to vote in its primaries and runoff primaries during the 2026-2027 election years. Since no political party provided a notification to the State Election Board Secretary by the statutory deadline, all primaries will remain closed for the 2026-2027 election years. Voters who would like to change their party affiliation should do so before April 1, 2026. State law prohibits party affiliation changes April 1 through August 31 of even-numbered years.

It lists July 31 as the voter-registration deadline and August 10 as the absentee-ballot request deadline. Early voting is scheduled for August 20–21 from 8 A.M. to 6 P.M. and August 22 from 8 A.M. to 2 P.M.
